newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials soar to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials soar to record highs.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks soared two percent to new highs on Thursday, boosted mainly by continuing high liquidity.
The main 57-share industrial index surged 224.25 points -- its single largest gain in a day -- to break through the 11,300 psychological barrier to close at a new all time high of 11,319.78.
"High liquidity is still giving the market momentum and I see it carrying it through to next week although sooner or later it might slow down but the undertone will still be firm," one broker said.

Another one said the market had also been given impetus by a lower than expected annual inflation figure of 21.4 percent in June and market players had also shrugged off concerns by weather experts of an early buildup of the El Nino phenomenon which they said could spark a possible drought in southern Africa.
"Some weather experts are saying it's a possibility that this El Nino will decline by the end of the year and the market at this stage is not reacting to it," he said.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Thursday, merchant bankers FMB surged 200 cents to 5,500, cigarette manufacturer BAT leapt 150 cents to 1,550, agricultural investor Chemco jumped 100 cents to 4,600 and hotels, supermarket and beverages conglomerate Delta rose 80 cents to 2,000.
Timber producer Border gained 50 cents to 1,650, clothing retailer Truworths added 50 cents to 730 and houses appliances-maker Capri put on 20 cents to 150.
Against the trend, steel windows and door-maker Radar dropped 25 cents to 500 and seed manufacturer and distributor SeedCo shed 20 cents to 420.

Minings continued dull with gold producer Ashanti jumping 1,000 cents to 9,000 despite a lower bullion fixing in London. Alloys preferentials were 10 cents easier at 60 and the mining index lost 12.55 points to 847.66.
